result.title: Learning What to Share: Expert Specialization for Time-Series Forecasting
result.summary: A central challenge in multivariate forecasting is deciding what to share across channels and where to specialize. Mixture-of-experts models offer flexible sharing, yet it remains unclear how much of their forecasting gains comes from added capacity or expert allocation. Through controlled comparisons across eleven datasets and three backbones, we show that informative channel assignments improve forecasting beyond matched shared capacity and random allocation. On frozen transformer backbones, persistent channel-specific mixtures outperform input-dependent routing on average. To examine when and how much specialization helps, we introduce GalaxyTS, a controlled synthetic dataset with exact shared and channel-specific forecasting references. It reveals how persistent channel mixtures exploit predictive differences concealed by short input windows and measures gains over matched shared corrections. These insights motivate Persistent Closed-Form Routing (PCR), a plug-and-play method that alternates exact conditional estimation of channel-specific mixture weights with gradient-based training of low-rank residual experts around a frozen pretrained forecaster. Averaged over four forecasting horizons, PCR-K4 achieves dataset-balanced mean squared error reductions of 3.86-14.25% relative to the three frozen backbones. In matched comparisons, PCR outperforms competing specialization methods on average while requiring substantially fewer trainable parameters.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究多变量时间序列预测中各通道该共享什么、何处该专门化：在 11 个数据集与 3 个 backbone 上做受控比较，区分增益来自容量还是专家分配，并提出合成数据集 GalaxyTS 与交替「闭式估计混合权重＋低秩残差专家训练」的 PCR 方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉或多模态推理无直接关联；但其对「新增容量 vs 路由分配」的受控分解、以及持久路由与输入依赖路由的对比，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态与额外计算的收益归因设计提供核查线索。
